title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Size of a Corrected Set
content:
This page settles how many originals a corrected set of `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` puts into circulation.

## Rule

1. **Full set.** When a corrected set does put originals into circulation, their number is the type's number of originals per set, in full.
2. **Otherwise nothing.** Each circumstance that the corrected-set rules describe as leaving the new set without originals prevails on its own: where one of them holds, the number is zero, regardless of the rest. The type's full number applies only where no such circumstance holds.
3. **Moment of reading.** Both the type's per-set number and the figures on the document are read at the time of the corrected issue itself, not earlier.
4. **Unit.** Only whole originals are counted; there are no fractions.

## Truth table

| Any circumstance leaving the new set without originals | Originals put into circulation |
|---|---|
| Yes | 0 |
| No | The type's originals per set |

## Worked examples (hypothetical)

- A corrected set on a type whose per-set number is taken to be 3, with no circumstance leaving it without originals: 3 originals go into circulation.
- The same type, but one circumstance leaving the set without originals holds: 0.
- A type with a per-set number of 0 would put nothing into circulation even when no such circumstance holds, because its full set is zero originals.
